Christmas adventure · ages 6 to 8

The Last Christmas Lantern

On Christmas Eve, every lantern on the village wall glows except one. Nell follows four tiny pawprints downhill to find out who needs its light.

Nell’s Christmas Eve

One for every wish

On Christmas Eve, everyone brought a lantern to the village wall. The baker wished for buns that never burned. Nell wished for snow all the way up to her knees. There was already enough to leak into one boot.

The last lantern

Nell counted the lights. Eleven. She counted the lanterns. Twelve. The one on the end was dark. She cupped her hands round its glass. The wick inside was cold. “Did somebody blow you out?” she whispered.

Four little toes

Something had brushed the snow off the wall. Below it lay a print with four little toes. Then another. Then a crooked line of them leading downhill. Nell called Gran over. Together, they followed the tracks.

Under the arch

By the old stone bridge, Nell heard a sneeze. An orange nose poked out from under the arch. A fox cub! It sniffed her mitten, sneezed again and gave a thin, squeaky bark.

An answer across the water

A fox barked back from the far bank. The cub skittered to the water’s edge and stopped. Its mother paced the opposite bank. Nell could see the black tips of her ears turn towards every squeak.

A bridge full of needles

A little way upstream stood a wooden footbridge. A spruce bough had fallen right across it. The cub tried to squeeze underneath, got a noseful of needles and backed out with its tail held stiff as a brush.

On the count of three

Gran called the neighbours. “Take the wide end,” said the baker. Nell brushed snow off the thinnest twigs. “One, two, THREE!” Up came the bough. Down came a shower of snow, straight into Nell’s other boot.

A light low down

The baker had brought the dark lantern. Gran lit its wick from hers. The cub waited at the bridge. Nell remembered how little it was. She held the light down by her knees and walked slowly, one bright board at a time.

Two red tails

Halfway over, the cub spotted those black-tipped ears. It shot past Nell and tumbled into its mother. She licked its snowy whiskers until they stuck out sideways. Nell sat very still. She wanted to remember those whiskers.

The twelfth light

“Shall we put it back?” asked Gran. Nell set the lantern at the foot of the bridge. From the hill she counted eleven lights on the wall and one small gold wink by the water. Twelve. “Merry Christmas, foxes,” she said.

Whose boots would you put in the snow?

Start with the Christmas lantern idea, add your reader’s name and choose who stars in their story. You can change the idea as you go.
